messages:
elaine: Circling back on the benchmark visuals. I mocked two approaches in figma: (1) compact sparkline pair (latency ms on left, cost $/1k tokens on right log-scale) and (2) slice chart that breaks cost into compute + memory + misc at three load points. Wanted opinions before we lock for the launch post + webinar slide.
sam: Both are useful. Sparkline works for hero social posts. Slice chart is great as a follow-up explainer for finance/dev-platform audiences. If we use slice, add a small legend for quantization+batching assumptions.
martin: Important: call out p50, p95 latency markers on the sparkline. Messaging should be "same latency, lower cost" not "faster and cheaper" unless we can prove both. Also recommend a short subline: "up to 3x token cost reduction at p95 vs baseline" (we'll source exact numbers).
tia: For the webinar: one slide to show the sparkline, next slide the slice chart teardown + live Q&A prompt about routing. I left slide notes with two CTA options: (A) book a Dedicated demo, (B) claim Hosted free trial. We'll A/B test headline copy for social meta.
elaine: Draft headline ideas in figma comments now. Trying to avoid the "speed vs price" trope. Options lean toward pragmatic: "Reduce inference spend without trading predictability" or shorter "Lower cost, predictable latency". Thoughts?
sam: Short headline wins on social. Use longer caption on page to explain test conditions. Also: use log scale on cost axis so the slice components don't look negligible.
martin: Routing detail: enterprises => Dedicated form (add a hidden field industry=enterprise), mid-market => sales-assist, startups/individuals => hosted free trial. Add UTMs: utm_campaign=bench_v1 & utm_variant=headlineA/B. Put these in the post links and webinar registration.
ops-bot: assets uploaded: https://cdn.redwood.ai/bench/v2/spark_slice_preview.png. Preview deployment: https://deployments.redwood.ai/preview/389
tia: Copywriter note: keep 1-line caption that says sample workload: T=1k tokens, batching=dynamic, quant=8-bit, run on T4-ish equivalent; link to appendix with full benchmark table. Also add a small footnote about synthetic prompts vs production mixes.
elaine: Quick visual ask for designer: annotate p50/p95 with small callouts, mark the percentile lines in grey, and add percent-savings callout bubble above the highest load point. Sam, martin - I added your comments.
sam: For analytics, we need two conversions: registration (webinar) + sales-intent (Dedicated form submitted). Martin, can your ops team add a UTM-to-sfdc mapping so we can attribute headline variant?
martin: Yup, I'll coordinate with ops. Also let's record a short 6-minute demo clip for the webinar landing page that shows live latency metrics — that boosts signups.
elaine: Meeting to finalize: tomorrow 11:00am PT. Deliverables before meeting: designer updates + CSV with p50/p95 numbers, headline A/B copy, CTA mapping. :thumbsup:
tia: Added two tweet-length snippets in figma comments and a 30s teaser script for the webinar.
elaine: Decisions so far: use sparkline as hero, slice chart as deep-dive, log-scale cost axis, percent-savings callout, CTA routing by customer tier with UTMs, A/B headline test. We'll lock final copy at tomorrow's meeting.
